title: Batch 49.7 on the 27B (L32), last in the queue: does the question's attention follow the written address? x8_write's routes scenes; at the bridge word none / the pointer swap 2 (mu_k - mu_j) / a random vector of its norm; softmax attention from the last token and the question tokens to every token at the full-attention layers > L (DeltaNet skipped and logged); five heads chosen on a fit half, read on the other; the best head zeroed (necessity); SEALED until Q49.7
command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.6-27b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x49_attn.py run --name x49_7_27b --why "batch 49, test 49.7 (jobs/c3/batch49.yaml with amendment 2; Q49.7): x8_write's items at L32, none / swap s = 2 / random of the swap's norm at the bridge word; attention at the full-attention layers > L from the last and question tokens; candidates on the fit half, the best head zeroed at the last / question tokens on the read half; sealed"
question: When the address at the bridge word is swapped (x8_write's mu_k - mu_j at s = 2), does the question's attention move onto the locker sentence of the written slot k, and does a head that moves carry the switch (zeroing it undoes it)?
why_it_matters: The address is probe-readable, removable and writable; nothing yet shows who dereferences it. A head whose attention follows the written address, and without which the switch falls, puts the dereference in hand at the head level; on the 27B, as on the 9B, three of four layers are Gated DeltaNet, so a null here may only say "not in full attention".

hypotheses.Q49.7: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q49.7, per model: (a) follows / (b) elsewhere / (c) neither; if (a), above L+4 or within 4 layers of L); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x49_attn.py verdict and view refuse until the Dan: line is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch49.yaml, 49.7, with amendment 2, Dan 28 Oct ~14:20). Read half, decisive query site the last token (the question tokens' mean beside, the same rules), cluster bootstrap over bridge entities (10,000, seed 0), EPS 1e-9 at the bars. move = (mass on slot k's sentence - mass on slot j's) under the arm minus the same under none, per head and (item, k); j = the bridge item's slot, k = the written slot; a sentence's mass = all its tokens. "The attention follows the address": on the pairs where the lookup switched to slot k's locker under the swap, >= 1 of the five candidate heads has mean move >= 0.30 with its CI excluding 0, its mean move under the random vector on the same pairs <= 0.05, and its mean move on the non-switched swap pairs <= 0.10. "Dereference elsewhere": the switch share >= 0.3 and no recorded head (every full-attention layer > L, every head) reaches a mean move of 0.15 on the switched pairs. Otherwise neither. (1) Aggregate, beside the per-head rule: the summed move over the five candidates and over every head of the best head's layer; "distributed dereference" if either sum >= 0.30 while no single candidate reaches 0.30. (2) Necessity: the best head (chosen on the fit half before the ablation runs) has its output (its slice of o_proj's input) zeroed at the last token, and separately at the question tokens, under the swap on the read half; "the head carries the position route" if the switch to slot k falls by >= 0.5 of its swap value while the identity answers (read pairs answering slot j's locker under the swap) change <= 0.10 and the recall's answer changes <= 0.10 (swap + zero vs swap); the clean answers lost (none + zero vs none) beside. (3) Weights-level, descriptive: S[k, k'] = (W_Q mu^q_k)^T (W_K mu^src_k') for the best head, mu^q_k = the mean last-token attention input (post input-norm) over items whose picked item is in slot k, mu^src_k' = the mean over items of the mean input at slot k''s locker-sentence tokens, unedited; diagonal dominance = (mean diagonal - mean off-diagonal) / SD of the off-diagonal; RoPE and the q/k norms left out (said so); the actual mean attention logits on slot j's / k's / the third sentence's tokens under none / swap / random beside. (4) The 9B caveat applies here too: if "elsewhere" holds (three of four layers are Gated DeltaNet), the verdict writes "the dereference is not in full attention on this model" and Muse decides. Report beside: the best head's layer and index (and L + how many), its attention entropy per arm, the per-token breakdown of its mass on slot k's sentence (item / number / rest), the total full-attention change (the summed move over every head; the mean total-variation distance from none over every head, swap vs random). As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override): items = x8_write.eligible (the routes test's C2 scenes, their O prompt, gate 0.80 per reader on O, the first 300; the run records whether they are x8's 300); fit / read halves by bridge entity (sorted, random.Random(0) shuffle, first half fit); candidates = the five (layer, head) with the most mass on the three locker sentences together at the last token under none, mean over fit items (ties: lower layer, then head); best head = the candidate with the largest mean move on the fit half's switched pairs (none switched: the first candidate); the lookup's answer read in the forward that records the attention (one prompt, X0's chat read), the recall and the ablation read with X0's batched chat read; swap / random classes as x8_write (target = slot k's digit, original = slot j's, third, other).
controls: a random vector of the swap's norm at the same token and layer, one per item and k (seed 4401, as x8_write): the move under it must stay <= 0.05 on the switched pairs
the non-switched swap pairs: the head's move there must stay <= 0.10 (a head that moves under any write is not following the address)
heads chosen on the fit half, every rule read on the other half (split by bridge entity, seed 0)
necessity: identity answers and the recall under the zeroed head (<= 0.10 changed each); the clean answers lost (none + zero vs none) beside
attention entropy per arm and the mean total-variation distance from none over every head, swap vs random (dumbest way 1); the item / number / rest split of slot k's mass (dumbest way 2)

title: Batch 49.2 on Muse (L26): the removal ladder. On the changed prompt of the clean one-pick scenes, the J++ part taken out at more and more tokens and layers (bridge word at L; L..L+3; + the item's mention; + the question; every token; Zach's top-10 at every token over L23-29), each beside a random subspace of the same share per token; both readers, both sentence orders
command: export BJ_TARGET=muse-glimmer-30b BJ_DEVICE_MAP= PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True; uv run python scripts/x49_ladder.py run --name muse30_x49_2_r2 --why "Batch 49, test 49.2 (jobs/c3/batch49.yaml and amendment 2; Q49.2): the removal ladder on S, clean design, rungs 1-6 (the bridge's Δ's 25 OMP atoms at L26, at L26..29 at the bridge word, + the item's mention, + the question's tokens, every token; Zach's top-10 per token over L23-29), random subspace of the same share per token beside each; sealed"
question: 47.5 took the J++ part out at one token and one layer and the recall kept 0.97; Zach's knock-out takes the top-10 lens directions out at every token over a band and the recall breaks. Where between the two does "follows" become "needs", and does the lookup ever need it?
why_it_matters: Decides between "the recall follows the J++ part" and "needs it" as the README's verb, and whether the gap to Zach's knock-out is the number of tokens (a second copy at the item's earlier mention, or the question) or the definition of the part (rung 5 vs rung 6: two definitions, not one).

hypotheses.Q49.2: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q49.2, per model: 9B; Muse; three P(yes)); not committed when this spec was written, so the job is sealed: per-item outputs only, no verdict; scripts/x49_ladder.py verdict refuses until the answer is committed.

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch49.yaml, 49.2, with amendment 2), verbatim: "The second copy is the earlier mention": rung (3) costs the recall >= 0.3 more than rung (2) in locker-first scenes (paired CI excluding 0) and rung (2) already costs >= 0.3 in locker-after scenes. "Needed only when everything goes": rungs (1)-(4) each <= 0.2 and rung (5) or (6) >= 0.5. "The lookup never needs it" if <= 0.1 beyond random at every rung. Design, verbatim: "Locker-first clean scenes (the earlier mention exists) and locker-after clean scenes (it does not); on S; zeroing (47.5's operation, per-layer lens and OMP), the random subspace of the same share beside each rung. Rungs: (1) bridge word, L; (2) bridge word, L..L+3; (3) + the item's earlier mention, L..L+3; (4) + the question's tokens, L..L+3; (5) every token, L..L+3; (6) every token, Zach's band (9B L12-16, Muse L23-29). Amendment 2: on rungs (3)-(5) the removal at tokens other than the bridge word is the projection onto the span of the same 25 atoms (the bridge item's lens identity wherever it appears), random of the same share per token; rung (6) uses Zach's top-10 per token via his code path. Both readers: share of S's answers kept." As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override before the run): scenes = each model's 45m run (x0_necessity --alt fresh, chat; the clean one-pick scenes: a locker item nobody picks becomes S's asked pick, only the bridge token differs), its eligible scenes at L (its gate passed; asserted), all of them (Muse: 409 = 178 locker-first + 231 locker-after; plan in results/x49_ladder/plan-*-muse30). Order = x0_strata's 'alt locker vs asked pick' (the new item's locker sentence, i.e. its earlier mention, before or after the asked pick; x45p's split); x45m's both-lockers group kept per item, descriptive. "The removal" at layer l = 47.5's zeroing: the state minus its projection on the span Q_l of the 25 signed-OMP atoms of Δ_l = h_S - h_O at the bridge word over the J++ lens's letter-token atoms at l (x0_parts.omp_atoms; X0's picks), on the state as it arrives; at every rung token the same Q_l (amendment 2). "The item's earlier mention" = the tokens of S's bridge item's name in its locker sentence (character offsets; 1-2 tokens); in locker-after scenes the same sentence after the pick is used (amendment 2's "wherever it appears"; the second-copy rule reads rung 2 there, so this does not touch the rule). "The question's tokens" = Zach's 'question' positions (ablate_v2.question_start onward: the question sentence, the template's tail and the read's appended token; ~28 on Muse). "Every token" = every token of the read prompt (~112, Muse's system turn included), the appended one included, no sink skipped. Random beside rungs 1-5: per token the first k columns of X0's random basis (seed 888 + l), k so they hold Q_l's share of that token's ||h_S||^2 on S's clean state at l (the reader's own read prompt). Rung 6 = ablate.removal_edit("top", LensDictionary(W_U[letters] * final-norm gain, J_l), [RowSettings(protected = the dictionary rows of S's clean read's top-10 tokens)], k = 10) at every token of L23..29 (ablate_v2's paper10 with --positions all, its dictionary built as ablate_v2 builds it), fp32 (TF32 off); random beside: per token random_subspace_part at the share his removal takes from the state as it arrives.
